title: Pseudo-coherence on an affine scheme is pseudo-coherence of the module complex
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules and let $E=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ be the corresponding object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\subseteq D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] under the affine equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Then $E$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $M^\bullet$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 08E7 (perfect-lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine, perfect.tex line 2223), pseudo-coherent clause

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$) Suppose $M^\bullet\cong F^\bullet$ in $D(A)$ with $F^\bullet$ a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules, $F^n\cong A^{r_n}$. Applying the functor of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] gives $E=\widetilde{M^\bullet}\cong\widetilde{F^\bullet}$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. Since $\widetilde A=\mathcal O_X$ (the equivalence sends $A$ to $\mathcal O_X$) and $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ commutes with finite direct sums [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction, part (4)], each $\widetilde{F^n}\cong\mathcal O_X^{r_n}$, so $\widetilde{F^\bullet}$ is a bounded-above complex of finite free $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Taking the one-member cover $\{X\}$ in [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], $E$ is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 08E7 proof, first sentence

proof.text: ($\Rightarrow$) Suppose $E$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]: every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with $E|_U\cong F_U^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ for a bounded-above complex $F_U^\bullet$ of finite free $\mathcal O_U$-modules. Standard opens form a basis and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is quasi-compact, so there are $f_1,\dots,f_n\in A$ with $X=\bigcup_i D(f_i)$ and each $D(f_i)$ inside some such $U$; restricting, $E|_{D(f_i)}\cong F_i^\bullet$ for a bounded-above complex $F_i^\bullet$ of finite free $\mathcal O_{D(f_i)}$-modules. Since the $D(f_i)$ cover $X$, the $f_i$ generate the unit ideal.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 08E7 proof, choice of a finite standard-open cover

proof.text: Fix $f=f_i$ and identify $D(f)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_f)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] the sections of $\widetilde N$ over each $D(g)\subseteq D(f)$ are $N_g=(N_f)_g$, compatibly with restriction and module structures, so $\widetilde N|_{D(f)}$ is the sheaf $\widetilde{N_f}$ on $\operatorname{Spec}(A_f)$ (both are sheaves agreeing on the basis of standard opens; Stacks, Schemes, discussion after Lemma lemma-spec-sheaves); termwise, $E|_{D(f)}=\widetilde{M^\bullet_f}$. Write $F_i^n=\mathcal O_{D(f)}^{r_n}=\widetilde{A_f^{r_n}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction, parts (1) and (2)] over $A_f$, $\operatorname{Hom}(\widetilde{A_f^{r}},\widetilde{A_f^{s}})=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_f}(A_f^r,A_f^s)$ via the functor, so the differentials of $F_i^\bullet$ are $\widetilde{d}$ for $A_f$-linear maps $d$ with $d\circ d=0$ (faithfulness); thus $F_i^\bullet=\widetilde{G^\bullet}$ for a bounded-above complex $G^\bullet$ of finite free $A_f$-modules. Now $\widetilde{G^\bullet}\cong\widetilde{M^\bullet_f}$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A_f})$, and [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] for the ring $A_f$ (full faithfulness) gives $M^\bullet_f\cong G^\bullet$ in $D(A_f)$.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 08E7 proof, "from the definition it follows that M_{f_i} is pseudo-coherent"

proof.text: By the previous step each $M^\bullet_{f_i}$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A_{f_i}$-modules, and the $f_i$ generate the unit ideal. By [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-localization-glue], $M^\bullet$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules.
